title: Plant the Studio Website Redesign

card.teaser: An e-commerce redesign that puts plants before promotions.

summary: An e-commerce UX/UI redesign exploring how clearer information architecture, more intuitive product discovery, and a plant-centered visual hierarchy can improve the online shopping experience.

hero.alt: Interactive Figma prototype of the Plant the Studio website redesign

text: Plant the Studio is an e-commerce redesign focused on making plant discovery more intuitive through clearer information and botanical visual storytelling
An e-commerce UX/UI redesign exploring how clearer information architecture, more intuitive product discovery, and a plant-centered visual hierarchy can improve the online shopping experience.

finalDesign: *Plants before promotions.* The old homepage opened on promo bars and a photo carousel. The redesign follows a single hero with four collections and a New This Week row, and every card shows its name, price, light and pot size. A visitor arriving from a restock post sees what's new within one scroll.

*One Plants page, in everyday words.* The old Plants menu split into insider labels like "TC" and "See What You're Buying." The redesign gathers the collections into tabs on one Plants page, renames tissue culture to Plantlets, and adds a sidebar that filters by light, care, type and size.

*Size and care on every card.* Product details used to sit under "More information." Each card now carries a spec line, such as BRIGHT INDIRECT · 6" POT · EXPERT, beneath the common name, genus and price, so shoppers can compare plants without opening each one.
*One sign-up, in one place.* Three sign-up prompts and a floating reward button compete for attention on every visit.
pull: I want something rare, but I need to know I won't kill it.
